hyps.why: Pushing an already large Adam learning rate further causes divergence and accuracy collapse.
Tiny learning rates leave the network undertrained in 243 epochs, so increasing them gives large gains.
Small batches already give noisy gradients and many updates, so raising the learning rate destabilizes training more.
Larger batches reduce the number of updates, which worsens undertraining when the learning rate is very small.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and help stabilize training at high learning rates.
At strong L2 penalties the model already underfits, so further increases shrink weights toward a trivial classifier.
Adding units helps most when the network is narrow and capacity-limited, with diminishing returns at large widths.
Reducing a divergent learning rate restores stable training and recovers accuracy.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to instability and dead units under large learning rates.
Relaxing a strong L2 penalty relieves underfitting, whereas at tiny alpha the change is negligible.
